meta.title: ProxMenux Post-Install: Optional Settings
meta.description: Guide to Optional Settings in the ProxMenux post-install script for additional Proxmox VE features and optimizations.
meta.ogDescription: Guide to Optional Settings in the ProxMenux post-install script for additional Proxmox VE features and optimizations.

title: Optional Settings
intro: The Optional Settings category provides additional features and optimizations that you can choose to apply to your Proxmox VE installation. These settings are not essential but can enhance your system's capabilities in specific scenarios.

ceph.title: Add Latest Ceph Support
ceph.intro: This option installs the latest Ceph storage system support for Proxmox VE. Ceph is a distributed storage system that provides high performance, reliability, and scalability.
doesItems: Adds the Ceph repository to your system
Updates package lists
Installs Ceph packages using the 'pveceph install' command
Verifies the installation
ceph.howUse: How to use: After installation, you can configure and manage Ceph storage using the Proxmox VE web interface or command-line tools.
ceph.automates: This adjustment automates the following commands:

amd.title: Apply AMD CPU Fixes
amd.intro: This option applies specific fixes for AMD EPYC and Ryzen CPUs to improve stability and compatibility.
doesItems: Detects if an AMD EPYC or Ryzen CPU is present
Applies kernel parameter 'idle=nomwait' to prevent random crashes (via /etc/kernel/cmdline on systemd-boot hosts, or /etc/default/grub on GRUB hosts — with a .bak of the original)
Configures KVM to ignore certain MSRs (Model Specific Registers) for better Windows guest compatibility
amd.howUse: How to use: These fixes are applied automatically and require a system reboot to take effect.
amd.automates: This adjustment automates the following commands:

ha.title: Enable High Availability Services
ha.intro: This option enables High Availability (HA) services in Proxmox VE, allowing for automatic failover of VMs and containers in case of node failure.
doesItems: Enables and starts the pve-ha-lrm (Local Resource Manager) service
Enables and starts the pve-ha-crm (Cluster Resource Manager) service
Enables and starts the corosync service for cluster communication
ha.howUse: How to use: After enabling these services, you can configure HA groups and resources in the Proxmox VE web interface.
ha.automates: This adjustment automates the following commands:

pveam.title: Update Proxmox VE Appliance Manager
pveam.intro: Refreshes the local index of container templates that pveam exposes in the Proxmox UI, so the list of available appliances is up to date the next time you create an LXC.
doesItems: Runs pveam update against the Proxmox mirrors to fetch the current appliance catalogue
Populates the appliance list shown by the web UI when creating a container
pveam.howUse: How to use: run it once when the appliance list in the UI feels stale, or after switching mirrors. It does not download the templates themselves — only the catalogue index.
pveam.automates: This adjustment automates the following command:

fastfetch.title: Install and Configure Fastfetch
fastfetch.intro: This option silently installs and configures Fastfetch, a system information tool that displays system specs and a custom logo at login.
doesItems: Silently downloads and installs the latest version of Fastfetch
Allows you to choose a custom logo (ProxMenux, Proxmox, Helper-Scripts, Home-Labs-Club, Proxmology, or a custom one)
Configures Fastfetch to display "System optimised by ProxMenux"
Sets up Fastfetch to run automatically at console login
fastfetch.importantBody: If you connect to Proxmox via SSH, you should select the Proxmox logo or create a custom one using jp2a or img2txt. The other logos are generated using chafa and may not display correctly in a standard SSH session.
fastfetch.customBody1: To use a custom logo, place your ASCII art text file in: /usr/local/share/fastfetch/logos/
fastfetch.customBody2: You can create custom logos using tools like chafa, jp2a, or img2txt.
customItems: Keep the logo height to 35 lines or less to maintain proportions and fit in the terminal
Use chafa for color logos (may not display correctly in SSH sessions)
fastfetch.automates: This adjustment automates the following commands:

figurine.title: Install and Configure Figurine
figurine.intro: This option installs and configures Figurine, a tool that creates stylish ASCII text banners for your terminal, displaying your hostname in a visually appealing 3D format.
doesItems: Downloads and installs Figurine v2.1.1 from GitHub for the host architecture (AMD64, ARM64 or ARMv7)
Creates a welcome message that displays your hostname in 3D ASCII art when you log in
Updates an existing Figurine binary after download and extraction succeed
Sets up the welcome message to run automatically at login
figurine.practicalBody: When managing multiple Proxmox nodes in a cluster, Figurine provides an immediate visual indication of which node you're currently logged into. This helps prevent accidental commands on the wrong node and improves your workflow when managing multiple servers.
figurine.automates: This adjustment automates the following process:
figurine.outro: After installation, you'll see your hostname displayed in 3D ASCII art each time you log in, making it immediately clear which Proxmox node you're working on.

log2ram.title: Install Log2RAM (SSD/NVMe wear reduction)
log2ram.intro: Log2RAM mounts /var/log on a tmpfs ramdisk and writes it to disk on a schedule, so the logs that change all the time, such as the pveproxy access log, are written to RAM instead of the root SSD. The journal and the task logs of Proxmox VE and Proxmox Backup Server stay on disk. A clean shutdown writes the ramdisk to disk; an abrupt power loss loses only the text logs written since the last sync.
doesItems: Detects whether the root disk is SSD/NVMe by reading /sys/block/<dev>/queue/rotational. On a rotational disk the Automated flow asks first before installing.

Installs Log2RAM 1.7.2 from the upstream project, checking that the download is that release, and leaves its code unchanged. Its error e-mail is turned off with NOTIFICATION=false, as Proxmox VE has no mail command by default.
Sizes the ramdisk based on host RAM: ≤ 8 GB → 128M, ≤ 16 GB → 256M, > 16 GB → 512M. Writes the value to SIZE= in /etc/log2ram.conf.

Keeps on disk the journal (/var/log/journal), the Proxmox VE task logs (/var/log/pve) and, where it is installed, the Proxmox Backup Server logs (/var/log/proxmox-backup), in /var/hdd.journal, /var/hdd.pve and /var/hdd.proxmox-backup. Each usual path becomes a link to its folder on disk. The move happens at boot, before Log2RAM starts.
Writes the ramdisk to disk with the Log2RAM timer every 1h / 3h / 6h according to the same RAM tier, and flushes the disk after each write, so a finished sync survives a power cut.

Installs a guard in /etc/cron.d/log2ram-auto-sync that runs every 10 minutes. When /var/log passes 85% of the ramdisk, it rotates the logs, compresses the ones just rotated and writes everything to disk. No log is emptied.

Keeps the systemd journal on disk with a 1 GB limit, in /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/proxmenux-log2ram.conf. On a host running Proxmox Backup Server, adds /etc/logrotate.d/proxmox-backup-api (20 MB × 3 rotation) for its API logs.

Registers itself in installed_tools.json so it can be reverted from Uninstall Optimizations. An update from an earlier version keeps the size and sync interval, and moves the journal to disk at the next boot.
log2ram.howUseBody: On the Automated flow Log2RAM installs unattended when an SSD/NVMe root is detected. The Customizable flow asks for size, sync interval and whether to enable the guard. The changes take effect at the next boot.
log2ram.verifyLabel: Verify and manage from the shell:
log2ram.verifyCode:
# Service state and sync timer
systemctl status log2ram
systemctl list-timers log2ram-daily.timer

# Ramdisk usage — /var/log IS the tmpfs itself
df -h /var/log

# Folders kept on disk, and the journal size
ls -l /var/log | grep -- '->'
journalctl --disk-usage

# Write the ramdisk to disk now
systemctl reload log2ram

# Current configuration
cat /etc/log2ram.conf
systemctl cat log2ram

# Recent Log2RAM activity
journalctl -u log2ram -n 50 --no-pager

zram.title: Enable ZRAM swap profile
zram.intro: Creates a compressed swap device in RAM, /dev/zram0, with systemd-zram-generator. Pages that the kernel moves to swap are compressed with zstd and kept in memory, so they are written to RAM before they reach the swap on disk.
doesItems: Installs systemd-zram-generator if it is missing, and records whether ProxMenux installed it.

Writes /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf.d/90-proxmenux.conf: a zram0 device sized to one tenth of the host RAM, zstd compression (zstd(level=9) with systemd-zram-generator 1.2.0 or later) and swap priority 32767.
With that priority the kernel fills ZRAM first. An existing swap on disk keeps its own priority and takes the pages that no longer fit in ZRAM.

Before changing anything, looks for another ZRAM setup: an active zram swap, a zram line in /etc/fstab, a systemd unit or another generator file. If it finds one, the option stops and leaves that setup as it is.
Starts dev-zram0.swap and checks that the active device matches the profile. If it does not, the previous state is restored.
Registers itself in installed_tools.json so it can be reverted from Uninstall Optimizations.
zram.howUseBody: The option is part of the Customizable flow only; the Automated flow does not apply it. The device is created again at every boot. While it is active, the Memory card of the ProxMenux Monitor shows its capacity, the swap used, the algorithm, the compression ratio and the physical memory it takes.
zram.verifyCode:
# Active swap devices and their priority
swapon --show

# ZRAM device: algorithm, size and compressed data
zramctl

# Profile written by ProxMenux
cat /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf.d/90-proxmenux.conf

# State of the swap unit
systemctl status dev-zram0.swap

autoApplication.title: Automatic Application
autoApplication.body: In the Customizable flow, select each optional feature according to your needs. Log2RAM is also part of the Automated flow with hardware detection; ZRAM remains Customizable-only. Review the individual sections for prompts and prerequisites.
